user: How do I build a database-driven Slackbot?
assistant: To build a database-driven Slackbot, you can follow the tutorial provided in the document at this link: <https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/solution-tutorials?topic=solution-tutorials-slack-chatbot-database-watson>. This tutorial will guide you through the process of building a Slackbot that allows you to search and create entries in a backend Db2 on Cloud database. The Slackbot is backed by the IBM Watson® Assistant service, and you will integrate Slack and IBM Watson® Assistant using an Assistant integration. Db2 on Cloud is made available to Watson Assistant as a custom extension.
user: Slack 
assistant: Slack is a cloud-based messaging application designed to facilitate collaboration among users. It serves as a platform that enables teams to connect and work together effectively. When you choose Slack as a service destination, any subscribed notifications about events can be sent as messages to specified Slack channels.
user: Configure the Slack integration
assistant: To configure the Slack integration for your assistant, follow these steps:
1. Navigate to the Integrations page by clicking the integrations icon in the left menu of your IBM Cloud account.  
2. Click "Add" on the Slack tile.  
3. Click "Confirm."  
4. Ensure that you have a Slack app to connect to. If you don't have one, create it by following the instructions in the "Starting with Slack apps" documentation.  
5. Open the Slack app in a new browser tab to easily switch back and forth between the Slack app settings page and the Watson Assistant Slack integration configuration page.  
6. On the settings page for your Slack app, go to the App Home page.  
7. Add access scopes for your Slack app by clicking the "Review Scopes to Add" or "Update Scopes" button.  
The method for Slack access has changed, so review the necessary scopes based on your app's requirements.
user: What is webhook?
assistant: A webhook is a mechanism that enables your program to send a request to an external application when a specific event occurs within your program.
user: How do I use it?
assistant: I do not have that information.

[The Start of Current Turn Question]
How can I make a programmatic call?
[The End of Current Turn Question]

[The Start of Reference Answer]
To make a programmatic call from a dialog node, you can follow the instructions in the document at this link: <https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/assistant-data?topic=assistant-data-dialog-webhooks>. This document provides information about how to define a webhook, invoke it from a dialog node, and handle errors. However, please note that you can define only one webhook URL for a dialog skill, and the service that you call from the webhook must return a response in 8 seconds or less.
Alternatively, if you want to call a client application from a dialog node, you can add a client action to your dialog node that pauses the dialog so a client-side process can run and return a result as part of the processing that occurs within a dialog turn. This feature was introduced with version 1.4, and you can find more information about it in the document at this link: <https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/assistant-data?topic=assistant-data-dialog-webhooks#client-action>.
In both cases, the programmatic call can be used to validate information, do calculations or string manipulations on user input, or get data from another application or service.

[The End of Reference Answer]

[The Start of Assistant's Answer]
To make a programmatic call through a webhook in Watson Assistant, invoke the webhook from one or more dialog nodes. A dialog skill supports only **one webhook URL**. [S8][S10]

For instructions, see [Making a programmatic call from dialog](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/assistant-data?topic=assistant-data-dialog-webhooks). The document identifies this approach for calling external services, such as a Cloud Functions web action. [S6]

If you use a **client application call** instead, specify the call name, parameter details, and error-message variable name according to the documented JSON formatting rules. This action does not execute the call directly: it pauses the dialog while your external client application performs the call and returns the result. [S1][S2][S3]

The supplied excerpts do not include the full webhook configuration procedure or JSON format.
[The End of Assistant's Answer]
